title: Daily Brain #003: three questions your gut gets wrong
notes: Checked by hand. Easy: passing the runner in 2nd puts you in 2nd; the runner in 1st is still ahead (classic riddle).
Medium: ball x, bat x + 1.00, 2x + 1.00 = 1.10 → x = 0.05. Ball 5¢, bat $1.05. With a 10¢ ball the bat is $1.10 and the total $1.20.
Hard: each machine makes 1 widget in 5 minutes, so 100 machines make 100 widgets in 5 minutes, working in parallel.

Medium and hard are items 1 and 2 of the Cognitive Reflection Test: Frederick, S. (2005). Cognitive Reflection and Decision Making. Journal of Economic Perspectives, 19(4), 25–42. 10¢ and 100 minutes are the intuitive wrong answers the test is built around.
Second solver: a different model, given only the questions and choices, answered 2nd, 5¢, 5 min.
Do not claim the test measures intelligence or that practising it makes you smarter.

scenes.title: Daily Brain #003: Answer fast
scenes.question: In a race, you pass the person in *2nd place*. What place are you in?
scenes.narration: Three questions, answer fast. You pass the runner in second place. What place are you in?
Second. You took their place. First is still ahead.

scenes.title: Daily Brain #003: Answer fast
scenes.question: A bat and a ball cost *$1.10*. The bat costs *$1.00 more* than the ball. How much is the ball?
scenes.narration: Medium. Together they cost one ten, and the bat costs a dollar more. How much is the ball?
Ball five cents, bat one oh five: together, one ten. A ten cent ball makes it one twenty.

scenes.title: Daily Brain #003: Answer fast
scenes.question: 5 machines make 5 widgets in 5 minutes. How long do *100 machines* take to make *100 widgets*?
scenes.narration: Hard. Five machines make five widgets in five minutes. How long for a hundred and a hundred?
Each machine makes one widget in five minutes. A hundred work at the same time.
What's your score out of six? Did ten cents get you?
